class.name: TransitionScreen
class.brief_description: Root of a scene that covers the screen while the next scene loads, then changes to it.
class.description: A transition screen is the root node of a scene you design like any other (a [ColorRect] background, a logo, a [ProgressBar]). Added to the [SceneTree], it runs one transition and frees itself: 1. On its first frame it emits [signal started] and starts loading [member next_scene] in the background with [method ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request] (and [member preload_assets] with [method ResourceDatabase.preload_from_list]). 2. It fades in over the current scene for [member fade_in_duration] seconds. 3. While fully visible it reports [signal load_progress] and emits [signal loaded] when everything is loaded. It waits at least [member min_duration] seconds (or until [method finish] is called, or a key, mouse button, touch or joypad button is pressed if [member skippable] is [code]true[/code]). 4. It changes the scene with [method SceneTree.change_scene_to_packed] while it is fully visible, so the old scene is never seen again. 5. It fades out over the new scene for [member fade_out_duration] seconds, emits [signal completed] and frees itself. The easiest way to start a transition is [method SceneTree.change_scene_with_transition]. A transition screen can also be the current scene (opened with [method SceneTree.change_scene_to_file], or the boot splash): it detaches itself from [member SceneTree.current_scene] before the change and stays for the fade-out. With an empty [member next_scene] it only fades in, waits and fades out, as an overlay. The fade modulates the whole layer (all children together, their own [member CanvasItem.modulate] stays untouched). Override [method _update_fade] for custom intro and outro animations. In the editor the screen is shown fully visible and does nothing. It runs while the tree is paused ([member Node.process_mode] is [constant Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS]). See [LoadingScreen] for a progress bar and tips, and [SplashScreen] for the boot splash. [b]Note:[/b] Without threads (the default Web export) the next scene loads in one blocking step while the screen is fully visible: animations on the screen pause during that step and [method get_progress] jumps from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. [b]Note:[/b] A [CanvasModulate] inside the screen replaces the fade, as both set the modulate of the layer's canvas.

method.name: _update_fade
finish
method.description: Changes the scene as soon as everything is loaded, without waiting for the rest of [member min_duration]. Needed when [member auto_finish] is [code]false[/code], for example for a "Press any key" prompt after [signal loaded].

method.name: get_fade
method.description: Returns the current visibility of the screen, from [code]0.0[/code] (transparent) to [code]1.0[/code] (fully visible).

method.name: get_progress
method.description: Returns the load progress of [member next_scene] from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. It is [code]1.0[/code] only when the scene and [member preload_assets] are loaded.

method.name: get_state
method.description: Returns the current step of the transition.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], the scene changes as soon as everything is loaded and [member min_duration] has passed. If [code]false[/code], the screen waits for [method finish] (or a skip input if [member skippable] is [code]true[/code]).
Seconds the screen takes to fade in over the current scene. [code]0.0[/code] shows it at once.
Seconds the screen takes to fade out over the new scene. [code]0.0[/code] hides it at once.

If [code]true[/code], the current scene is freed as soon as the screen is fully visible, and [member next_scene] starts loading only then. The old and the new scene are never in memory together, which helps on mobile and Web; loading starts a little later.
Minimum seconds the screen stays fully visible before the scene changes, even if loading is done earlier.

Path or UID of the scene to change to. If empty, no scene change happens: the screen fades in, waits [member min_duration] and fades out. [SplashScreen] uses [member ProjectSettings.application/run/main_scene] instead. A screen never loads its own scene file.

Optional assets that are loaded into the [ResourceDatabase] with [method ResourceDatabase.preload_from_list] while the screen loads [member next_scene]. The scene changes only after [signal ResourceDatabase.preload_finished] for this list.
If [code]true[/code], a pressed key, mouse button, touch or joypad button emits [signal skipped] and calls [method finish]. The scene still changes only when everything is loaded.

signal.name: completed
signal.description: Emitted when the screen has faded out over the new scene, right before it frees itself.

signal.name: load_progress
signal.description: Emitted when the load progress changes, with a value from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code]. See [method get_progress].

signal.name: loaded
signal.description: Emitted once when [member next_scene] and [member preload_assets] are loaded (also when loading failed; the current scene then stays).

signal.name: skipped
signal.description: Emitted when a skip input was pressed while [member skippable] is [code]true[/code].

signal.name: started
signal.description: Emitted on the first frame of the screen in the tree, when loading starts and the fade-in begins.

constants.constant: Not started yet (or in the editor).
Fading in over the current scene.
Fully visible, everything loaded; waiting for [member min_duration] or [method finish].
The scene has changed; fading out over the new scene.
Done; the screen is freed at the end of the frame.
